items.title: The 2 pi-periodic three-torus, its normalized measure, test functions and the Sobolev spaces H^s
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

items.title: Finite speed of propagation for linear symmetric hyperbolic systems: cone domination and independence of the extension
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), carrying the hypotheses of the analytic suppliers used below.

Let $T>0$, let $A^\mu:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
($\mu=0,1,2,3$) be smooth with $A^0(t,x)\ge aI$ for some constant $a>0$ and all
$(t,x)$, and let $\|A^i(t,x)\|\le b$ for the operator norm and all $i,t,x$. Let
$C:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to M_m(\mathbb R)$ be smooth and bounded by $K$.

**(a)** Put $\lambda:=\sqrt3\,b/a+1$; then $\lambda A^0(t,x)+\xi_iA^i(t,x)\ge0$ as a
quadratic form for every $(t,x)$ and every $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$|\xi|\le1$.

**(b)** Let $w\in C^1((-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ solve
$$A^0\partial_tw+A^i\partial_iw+Cw=0 ,$$
and let $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, $0<t_0<T$, and suppose $w(0,x)=0$ for every
$|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$. Then $w(t,x)=0$ for every
$(t,x)\in\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ |x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$.

**(c)** [independence of the extension] If $w_1,w_2$ are two solutions of two
such systems whose complete coefficient families, including $C$, agree on an open set containing the
truncated cone $D=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,|x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$, and if
$w_1(0,x)=w_2(0,x)$ for $|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$, then $w_1=w_2$ on $D$.

items.title: Uniform quadratic-form bounds for positive definite symmetric matrices and smoothness of the inverse
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

items.title: Locally uniform extraction for X_1-bounded, X_0-Lipschitz families with compact X_1-bounded subsequences
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X_0$ be a complete normed space over
$\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ ([[def-banach-space]],
[[def-complete-metric-space]]) and let $X_1\subseteq X_0$ be a linear subspace
carrying a norm $\|\cdot\|_1$ such that ([[def-normed-subspace]]):

**(i)** there is $\kappa\ge0$ with $\|x\|_0\le\kappa\|x\|_1$ for every
$x\in X_1$; and

**(ii)** every sequence in $X_1$ bounded in $\|\cdot\|_1$ has a subsequence
converging in $X_0$ ([[def-metric-convergence]]).

Let $T>0$, $R\ge0$, $C\ge0$, and for $j\in\mathbb N$ let
$f_j:(-T,T)\to X_1$ satisfy
$$\|f_j(t)\|_1\le R,\qquad \|f_j(t)-f_j(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ j\in\mathbb N).$$

Then there are a strictly increasing sequence $j_1<j_2<\cdots$ in $\mathbb N$
and a continuous map $f:(-T,T)\to X_0$ ([[def-continuous-map-top]]) such that
$f_{j_n}\to f$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$; moreover
$\|f(t)-f(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|$ for all $t,t'\in(-T,T)$.

items.title: Periodic Fourier differentiation identity and equivalence of the derivative and Fourier-weight Sobolev norms
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$,
$\widehat u(k)$, the weak derivatives $D^\alpha$ and the spaces
$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]], and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2,\qquad |k|^2:=k_1^2+k_2^2+k_3^2 .$$

**(a)** Let $u\in H^s$ and let $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with $|\alpha|\le s$. Then
$D^\alpha u\in H^{s-|\alpha|}$ and
$$\widehat{D^\alpha u}(k)=(ik)^\alpha\,\widehat u(k)\qquad(k\in\mathbb Z^3),\qquad (ik)^\alpha:=\prod_{j=1}^3(ik_j)^{\alpha_j}.$$

**(b)** Let $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ satisfy $N_s(u)<\infty$.
Then $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$, and there are constants
$0<c_s\le C_s<\infty$, depending only on $s$, such that
$$c_s\,N_s(u)^2\le\|u\|_{H^s}^2\le C_s\,N_s(u)^2 .$$
The right-hand inequality holds for every $u\in H^s$, so the two norms are
equivalent on $H^s$.

items.title: Fourier modes on the periodic three-torus and the Galerkin projection P_N
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$ and the
spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] ($m\ge1$).

**(a) Mode sets.** For $N\ge0$ put
$\Lambda_N:=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3:|k|\le N\}$ with $|k|$ the Euclidean norm, and
$$X_N:=\Bigl\{\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}a_k\chi_k:\ a_k\in\mathbb C^m,\ a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}\Bigr\}\subseteq C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m),$$
the **Galerkin space of modes up to $N$**; it is a finite-dimensional real
vector space of dimension $d_N:=m\,|\Lambda_N|$, and $X_N\subseteq X_{N'}$ for
$N\le N'$. (The reality condition $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$ is exactly the
condition that the trigonometric polynomial be real-valued.)

**(b) Projection.** For $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ define
$$P_Nu:=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k,\qquad (P_Nu)(x)=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k(x),$$
with $\widehat u(k)$ the Fourier coefficients of clause (c) of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]; the second expression is a finite
sum, so $P_Nu\in X_N$; and $P_N:X_N\to X_N$ is the identity.
$P_N$ is called the **Galerkin (Fourier) projection**.

The definition fixes the projection only. Its self-adjointness,
derivative-commutation and operator-norm properties are proved in
[[lem-gr-galerkin-projection-properties]].

items.title: Periodic first-order symmetric hyperbolic systems: coefficients, admissible values, data classes and solutions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $m\ge1$, an open set
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with the subspace topology and a nondegenerate open
interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$. All functions on
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ are those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and smoothness on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ means smoothness of the
representative in the sense of clause (e) of that item.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

**(b) The system.** The associated **symmetric hyperbolic system** is
$$A^0(t,x,u)\,\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\,\partial_iu+B(t,x,u)=0 .\qquad(\star)$$

**(c) Values and norms.** A map $u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
on an interval $J$ **takes values in a set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$** when
$u(t)(x)\in E$ for every $t\in J$ and every $x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with
$u(t)$ read through its continuous representative when $s>3/2$. For compact
$K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$ put
$$\mathcal S(K,R):=\bigl\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ takes values in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\bigr\}.$$

**(d) Classical solutions.** Let $s\ge2$. A **classical solution of $(\star)$ on
$J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$** is a $C^1$ map
$u:J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^m$ with $u(t,x)\in O$ for all
$(t,x)$ and $(\star)$ satisfied at every point, such that
$u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)$ and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$. (For $s\ge2$
the embedding clause gives a continuous representative, so the pointwise
conditions are meaningful.)

**(e) Sobolev solutions.** Let $s\ge5$ and let $J$ be an open interval. A map
$u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ is a **Sobolev solution of
$(\star)$ on $J$** when

1. $u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$ and the distributional time
   derivative $\partial_tu$ lies in $L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$;
2. $u$ takes values in $O$;
3. for almost every $t\in J$ the identity $(\star)$ holds in
   $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, the coefficients being composed with
   the continuous representative of $u(t)$; all products are defined because
   $A^0(t,\cdot,u(t))$ and $A^i(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lie in $H^s$ with norm bounded
   by a function of $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$, $\partial_tu(t)$ and $\partial_iu(t)$ lie
   in $H^{s-1}$, and $B(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lies in $H^s$.

**(f) Initial data.** **Initial data for $(\star)$ at time $0$** are a class
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $s\ge5$ whose values lie in a
compact subset of $O$; a solution **has initial value $u_0$** when
$u(t)\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ as $t\to0$ within $J$.

The definition introduces the system and its solution classes only; existence,
uniqueness, continuous dependence and smooth persistence are asserted and
proved in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]],
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] and
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

items.title: Completeness of the periodic Sobolev spaces H^s(T^3_{2 pi}; R^N)
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge0$ be an integer and $N\ge1$, write
$H^s=H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ for the periodic Sobolev space with
its norm $\|\cdot\|_{H^s}$ and Fourier coefficients
$\widehat u(k)\in\mathbb C^N$ of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2\le+\infty .$$
Then:

**(a)** every Cauchy sequence in $(H^s,\|\cdot\|_{H^s})$ converges in
$(H^s,\|\cdot\|_{H^s})$; that is, $H^s$ is a real Banach space;

**(b)** more precisely, for every Cauchy sequence $(u_n)$ in $H^s$ there is
$u\in H^s$ with $N_s(u_n-u)\to0$, and then
$\|u_n-u\|_{H^s}\le C_s^{1/2}N_s(u_n-u)\to0$, where $C_s$ is the constant of
clause (b) of
[[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]]; this $u$ is
the unique limit of $(u_n)$.

items.title: Periodic Sobolev embedding: H^s on the three-torus controls C^m when s minus m exceeds three halves
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

items.title: The Galerkin projection is self-adjoint, commutes with derivatives, is a contraction in every H^r, converges to the identity and has the sharp Fourier-tail bound
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

items.title: The periodic Sobolev space H^k of the three-torus is a Banach algebra for k at least four
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $k\ge4$ be an integer and let
$u,v\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** For every $|\gamma|\le k-2$ the weak derivative $D^\gamma u$ has a
continuous representative and
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}|D^\gamma u(x)|\le C_k\|u\|_{H^k},$$
with $C_k$ depending only on $k$;

**(b)** the pointwise product $uv$ of the continuous representatives lies in
$H^k$ and
$$\|uv\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|u\|_{H^k}\,\|v\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** if $\varphi\in C^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and
$w\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, then $\varphi w\in H^k$ and
$$\|\varphi w\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|\varphi\|_{C^k}\,\|w\|_{H^k}.$$

items.title: Smooth composition, difference, coefficient product and commutator estimates on bounded H^s data
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

items.title: The Galerkin system is a smooth finite-dimensional ODE: local existence, smooth dependence and the continuation criterion
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open,
let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family on $O$ over
an open interval $I\ni0$ ([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in a compact
$K\subseteq O$ with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$, and let $P_N$, $X_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and space ([[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]). Fix $N\ge0$ for which $P_Nu_0$ takes values in $O$. Then:

**(a)** there is an open interval $J_N\ni0$ and a $C^1$ map $u_N:J_N\to X_N$
such that for all $t\in J_N$
$$P_N\Bigl[A^0(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_tu_N(t)+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_iu_N(t)+B(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\Bigr]=0\quad\text{in }L^2,$$
with $u_N(0)=P_Nu_0$;

**(b)** [continuation criterion] if $[0,T_*)$ is the forward-maximal interval of
existence of $u_N$ and there are a compact $C\subseteq O$ and a constant
$R_1\ge0$ with $u_N(t)$ taking values in $C$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t\in[0,T_*)$, and $T_*\in I$, then $u_N$ does not have $T_*$ as a finite forward endpoint:
the solution extends beyond $T_*$;

**(c)** the solution is unique and its local flow depends smoothly on the
finite-dimensional coordinates of the initial data.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, fix a compact interval $I_0$ inside the coefficient time domain, and assume $J\subseteq I_0$. Let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let $K\subseteq O$ be compact
and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution of
[[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]] for some $N\ge0$. Suppose that
$u_N(t)$ takes values in $K$ and satisfies $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for every
$t\in J$. Then there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,I_0)$ such that for every
$0\le j\le s-1$ and every $t\in J$
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)\|_{H^j}\le C\,\bigl(1+\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\bigr).$$

items.title: Dust reduction variables: signature flip, frame, connection, kinematics, comoving-parallel gauge and unknowns
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
signature $(-+++)$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Fix mathematical
parameters $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. On an open set
$U_0\subseteq M$, prescribe a smooth function $\rho\ge0$ and a smooth
future-directed unit timelike field $u$, with $g(u,u)=-1$. Set
$\varepsilon:=\rho c^2$ and $T^{ab}:=\varepsilon u^au^b$. On the open positive
subset $\{\rho>0\}$, the tuple $(\varepsilon,u)$, rather than $(\rho,u)$, is
exactly the dust model of [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]: that supplier's density
is the coefficient of $u\otimes u$. Here $\rho$ denotes its mass-normalized
parameter and $\varepsilon$ its energy-normalized coefficient. On zero-density
regions the smooth unit field is prescribed separately; the geodesic equation
is imposed there as well and is not deduced from conservation of the zero
tensor. This is the smooth geodesic-dust extension, without a free boundary
or a division by density. Make the following
**reduction conventions**, all local to an open set $U\subseteq U_0$:

**(a) Signature flip.** Put $\gamma:=-g$, a smooth metric of signature
$(+---)$ on $U$, with inverse $\gamma^{-1}=-g^{-1}$; all indices in the
reduction are raised and lowered with $\gamma$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). Put
$$U:=u,\qquad r:=\rho c^2 .$$
Then $\gamma(U,U)=1$. Whenever the mathematical model equation
$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds, it reads
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat_\gamma\otimes U^\flat_\gamma$ with
the same constant $\kappa$ and the Einstein tensor of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Indeed the constant metric
flip leaves the connection and mixed curvature unchanged, so Ricci is unchanged,
the scalar changes sign and $G(\gamma)=G(g)$; both lower factors in $T$
change sign together. The original metric is recovered by $g=-\gamma$.
Physical identification of these mathematical parameters is made by the
consuming physical model, not assumed by this definition.

**(b) Orthonormal frame.** Choose a smooth orthonormal frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ on $U$ with $e_0=U$ and
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}:=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)_{ij}$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
Its connection coefficients are defined by
$$\nabla_ie_j=\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j\,e_k,\qquad \Gamma_{ijk}:=\gamma_{kl}\Gamma_i{}^l{}_j=-\Gamma_{ikj},$$
and the frame components of $U$ are $U^i=\delta^i_0$.
The **spatial projection** onto the $\gamma$-orthogonal complement of $U$ and the tensor
$$h_{ij}:=\gamma_{ij}-U_iU_j,\qquad l_{ij}:=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$$
coincide with $\gamma$-orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$
when restricted to spatial pairs.

**(c) Kinematics.** With $\nabla$ the metric connection of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) put
$$\chi_{ij}:=h_i{}^k\nabla_kU_j,\qquad \chi:=h^{ij}\chi_{ij},\qquad \chi^{ij}:=h^{ik}h^{jl}\chi_{kl},$$
and let $D$ denote fully projected covariant differentiation: for a spatial
tensor field $T$, $(DT)_{i\ldots}:=(h_i{}^j\cdots)\nabla_j(T_\ldots)$, so
$D_ih_{jk}=0$ and $D_i\epsilon_{jkl}=0$. Let $\epsilon_{ijkl}$ be the
$\gamma$-volume tensor with $\epsilon_{0123}=1$ and set
$\epsilon_{ijk}:=\epsilon_{0ijk}$ (so $\epsilon_{123}=1$).

**(d) Comoving-parallel gauge.** Assume the coordinates
$(x^0=s,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ on $U$ are **comoving** ($e_0=\partial_s$ and $x^\alpha$
constant along the flow lines of $e_0$, $s$ a parameter on them) and
**parallel** ($\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$, i.e. the spatial frame is parallelly
transported along $U$). This gauge is admissible for tilted configurations: the
initial surface $s=0$ is the given spacelike surface and need not be orthogonal
to $U$.

**(e) Unknowns.** The unknowns of the reduction are the coefficients
$$u_{\mathrm{red}}:=\bigl(e_a{}^\mu,\ \Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,\ E_{ij},\ B_{ij},\ r\bigr),\qquad a=1,2,3,$$
where $E$ and $B$ are the electric and magnetic parts of the Weyl curvature
defined in [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]; the transport,
evolution and subsidiary equations they satisfy are stated and derived in
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]],
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]],
[[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

During the independent reduced evolution, the frame and the coefficients
$\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j$ are tentative smooth unknowns. The coefficients define a
metric-compatible connection by $\widehat\nabla_{e_a}e_j=\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j e_i$
and the tensor product rule; impose the same coefficient antisymmetry and
parallel gauge, but do not assume its torsion vanishes or that it is the
metric-selected connection. In reduction calculations $\nabla$ denotes this
tentative connection. The residual theorem establishes that it equals the
metric-selected connection for constrained solutions. The frame is required
to remain a basis, so it defines the tentative metric by its constant
orthonormal components.

items.title: Compactness of H^r-bounded families in H^{r-1} and locally uniform H^{s-1} subsequences of Galerkin solutions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(a)** For every integer $r\ge1$, every $R\ge0$ and every sequence $(v_j)$
in $H^r(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $\|v_j\|_{H^r}\le R$ there is a
subsequence converging in $H^{r-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$.

**(b)** Let $s\ge5$, $R\ge0$, $T>0$ with the compact slab $[-T,T]$ contained in the coefficient time domain $I$, let $K\subseteq O$ be compact, and let
$u_N:(-T,T)\to X_N$ ($N\in\mathcal N$), where $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ is any infinite set of Fourier cutoffs be a family of Galerkin solutions with
$u_N(t)$ taking values in $K$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$. Then the
family is equicontinuous in the $H^{s-1}$ metric: there is
$C_0=C_0(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,[-T,T])$ with
$$\|u_N(t)-u_N(t')\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_0\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ N\in\mathcal N).$$

**(c)** Under the hypotheses of (b) there are a strictly increasing sequence
$N_j\in\mathcal N$, $N_j\to\infty$ and $u\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m))$
with $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$ in the
$H^{s-1}$ norm.

items.title: Equivalence of the weighted Galerkin energy with the H^s norm and its Gronwall inequality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, fix a compact interval $I_0$ inside the coefficient time domain, and assume $J\subseteq I_0$. Let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin
solution ([[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]]) with $u_N(t)$ taking values
in $K$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t\in J$. Define the **weighted
energy**
$$e(t):=\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl(D^\alpha u_N(t)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}A^0\bigl(t,x,u_N(t)\bigr)\bigl(D^\alpha u_N(t)\bigr)\,d\mu(x).$$
Then:

**(a)** there are $0<a\le b$, depending on $A^0$, $K$, $s$ and $I_0$, with
$a\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}^2\le e(t)\le b\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}^2$ for all $t\in J$;

**(b)** $e$ is $C^1$ on $J$ and there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,I_0)$ with
$$|e'(t)|\le C\,\bigl(1+e(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J).$$
Consequently $e(t)\le(1+e(t_0))e^{C|t-t_0|}$ for $t,t_0\in J$ by Gronwall's inequality.

items.title: Uniform H^{s-2} Lipschitz bound for the time derivative of a Galerkin solution
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $I_0$ be a compact interval inside the coefficient time domain, and let $K\subseteq O$ be compact. Let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution, with $J\subseteq I_0$, values in $K$ and $\|u_N\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then, uniformly in $N$,
$$\|\partial_t^2u_N(t)\|_{H^{s-2}}\le C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,I_0),$$
and consequently
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)-\partial_tu_N(t')\|_{H^{s-2}}\le C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,I_0)|t-t'|.$$
No convexity of $K$ is required.

items.title: The barotropic enthalpy variable r(epsilon): definition, strict monotonicity and the symmetric form of the fluid equations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the integral below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let a perfect-fluid model on a Lorentzian manifold
be given with smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ defined on an open
interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0$ and
$p'(\epsilon)>0$ for all $\epsilon\in J$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Fix a base point
$\epsilon_*\in J$ and define the **barotropic enthalpy variable**
$$r:J\to\mathbb R,\qquad r(\epsilon):=\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon}\frac{\sqrt{p'(z)}}{z+p(z)}\,dz .$$
The integrand is continuous on $J$ ([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]), so
$r$ is well defined and $C^1$ with $r'(\epsilon)=\sqrt{p'(\epsilon)}/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))>0$
([[cor-ftc-integral-function-differentiable-almost-everywhere]]); hence $r$
maps $J$ diffeomorphically onto the open interval $r(J)$, and we write
$\epsilon(r)$ for its inverse and $c_s:=\sqrt{p'}$ for the **sound-speed
function**, so that $r'(\epsilon)=c_s(\epsilon)/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))$ and
$c_s\in(0,1)$ when $0<p'<1$ is assumed.

The definition and the two displayed equivalences are the form in which the
fluid system is fed into [[lem-gr-barotropic-fluid-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]];
no existence theorem is asserted here.

items.title: Schouten tensor, prescribed curvature, electric-magnetic Weyl variables and the reconstruction formula in the dust reduction
items.statement:
Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]: $\gamma$ is the signature
$(+---)$ metric, $U$ the unit future timelike vector $U=n$, $r=\rho c^2$, the
frame $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\gamma$-orthonormal with $e_0=U$,
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}$ on spatial pairs, and indices are moved with
$\gamma$.

**(a) Schouten tensor.** The **reduction Schouten tensor** of $\gamma$ is
$$S_{ij}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\tfrac16S_\gamma\,\gamma_{ij},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $S_\gamma=\gamma^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are
the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the dust field equation
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat\otimes U^\flat$ holds, then
$$S_{ij}=\kappa r\Bigl(U_iU_j-\tfrac13\gamma_{ij}\Bigr)-\tfrac13\Lambda\,\gamma_{ij}.$$
This normalization is fixed so that the standard Kulkarni--Nomizu decomposition
$$R_{ijkl}=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr)$$
holds for every metric of dimension four, with $C$ the Weyl tensor
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]); the identity is checked on
constant-curvature metrics in the Remarks.

**(b) Prescribed curvature.** The **prescribed curvature tensor** of a
configuration $(C,E,B,r)$ is the tensor field with frame components
$$R^{\mathrm{pre}}{}_{ijkl}:=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr),\qquad S_{ij}\text{ as in (a)} ,$$
where $C=C[E,B]$ is the Weyl tensor reconstructed from the electric and
magnetic variables in (d). A **tentative reduced configuration** is a smooth assignment
$(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ in the gauge of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Equality of its actual curvature
with $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ is the curvature constraint, rather than an assumption
on the independent unknowns. Reduced evolution enforces its time components;
the residual theorem establishes the remaining components from constrained
initial data. This distinction keeps the tentative connection available before
torsion-freeness and the full curvature constraint are proved.

**(c) Electric and magnetic Weyl variables.** For a smooth Weyl-type tensor $C$
of type $(0,4)$ with the curvature symmetries write
$C^*{}_{ijkl}:=\tfrac12C_{ij}{}^{pq}\epsilon_{klpq}$ for its right dual
([[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] clause (c) for
$\epsilon_{ijkl}$). The **electric and magnetic parts with respect to $U$** are
the spatial fields
$$E_{ij}:=C_{0i0j},\qquad B_{ij}:=C^*{}_{0i0j},$$
with frame indices; they are symmetric and spatial in all indices and
trace-free with respect to $h$ whenever $C$ has the Weyl symmetries.

**(d) Reconstruction formula.** Define the dependent tensor
$$C_{ijkl}:=2\bigl(l_{j[k}E_{l]i}-l_{i[k}E_{l]j}\bigr)-2\bigl(U_{[k}B_{l]p}\epsilon^p{}_{ij}+U_{[i}B_{j]p}\epsilon^p{}_{kl}\bigr),$$
with brackets of weight $\tfrac12$ and $l_{ij}=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$; this expression
is the **reconstruction** of a Weyl tensor from a pair $(E,B)$ of symmetric
spatial trace-free fields. The verification that the reconstructed tensor has
the curvature antisymmetries, pair symmetry, cyclic identity and zero traces —
and that its electric and magnetic parts recover $(E,B)$ — is the content of
[[lem-gr-dust-weyl-reconstruction-from-electric-magnetic]].

The definition fixes the objects and conventions only; the evolution and
subsidiary equations, the initial-data determination and the local existence
theorem are proved in the items named above and in
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]].

items.title: A limit of Galerkin solutions is a Sobolev and then a classical solution of the symmetric hyperbolic system
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq K_1\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Let $T>0$ with $[-T,T]$ contained in the coefficient time domain, let $N_j\to\infty$ be strictly
increasing, and let $u_{N_j}:(-T,T)\to X_{N_j}$ be Galerkin solutions with
$u_{N_j}(0)=P_{N_j}u_0$, values in $K_1$ and $\|u_{N_j}(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t$, such that $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of
$(-T,T)$ in $H^{s-1}$ (as provided by [[lem-gr-galerkin-compactness]] clauses
(b) and (c)). Then:

**(a)** $u(t)\in H^s$ for every $t$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C_{R_1}$ with
$C_{R_1}$ independent of $t$; $u$ takes values in $K_1$; and
$u\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1})\cap L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)$;

**(b)** the distributional time derivative $\partial_tu$ is represented by a
function in $L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1})$ and
$\|\partial_tu\|_{L^\infty H^{s-1}}\le C(C_{R_1})$;

**(c)** $u$ satisfies the system $(\star)$ of
[[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]] in the sense of Sobolev
solutions, and in fact $u\in C^1((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$ and solves
$(\star)$ classically with $u(0)=u_0$.

items.title: Tentative coframe, Cartan torsion and curvature, and the curvature residual of the dust reduction
items.statement:
Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]], with a smooth tentative frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, $e_0=U$, dual coframe $\theta^i(e_j)=\delta^i_j$ and smooth
metric-compatible tentative connection coefficients $\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j$.
The connection acts on every tensor index by the tensor product rule and
annihilates $\gamma$; torsion-freeness is not assumed. A differential $k$-form
is a smooth alternating covariant $k$-tensor. The wedge is its alternating
tensor product, normalized so that for a $p$-form $\alpha$ and a $q$-form
$\beta$, $\alpha\wedge\beta$ is the sum over $(p,q)$ shuffles with their signs.
The exterior derivative is specified, for smooth fields $X_0,\ldots,X_k$, by
$$d\alpha(X_0,\ldots,X_k)=\sum_{a=0}^k(-1)^aX_a\bigl(\alpha(X_0,\ldots,\widehat X_a,\ldots,X_k)\bigr)+\sum_{a<b}(-1)^{a+b}\alpha([X_a,X_b],X_0,\ldots,\widehat X_a,\ldots,\widehat X_b,\ldots,X_k).$$
Here a hat deletes a slot, and the undeleted slots in the second sum retain
their order. These definitions fix the local frame-coordinate calculus.

**(a) Connection forms.** The **connection $1$-forms** are
$\omega^i{}_j:=\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j\,\theta^k$, and the **torsion $2$-forms** and
**curvature $2$-forms** are the Cartan expressions
$$\Theta^i:=d\theta^i+\omega^i{}_j\wedge\theta^j,\qquad \Omega^i{}_j:=d\omega^i{}_j+\omega^i{}_k\wedge\omega^k{}_j .$$
Components are denoted
$\Theta^i=\tfrac12\Theta^i{}_{jk}\theta^j\wedge\theta^k$ and similarly for
$\Omega$. The actual curvature uses the frame bracket in its component formula:
$R^i{}_{jkl}=\partial_k\Gamma_l{}^i{}_j-\partial_l\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j+\Gamma_k{}^i{}_m\Gamma_l{}^m{}_j-\Gamma_l{}^i{}_m\Gamma_k{}^m{}_j-\Gamma_m{}^i{}_j\,[e_k,e_l]^m$,
not the antisymmetrized connection coefficients alone, precisely so that no
torsion conclusion is assumed.

**(b) Curvature residual.** With the prescribed curvature $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$
of [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]] the
**curvature residual $2$-forms** are
$$\Delta^i{}_j:=\Omega^i{}_j-\tfrac12R^{\mathrm{pre}\,i}{}_{jkl}\,\theta^k\wedge\theta^l .$$

**(c) Bianchi and matter residuals.** Using the reconstructed $C$ and
prescribed $S$ of [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]],
define
$$F_{jkl}:=\nabla_i\bigl(C^i{}_{jkl}-\delta^i{}_{[k}S_{l]j}\bigr),\qquad q_j:=\nabla_i(rU^iU_j),\qquad q:=U(r)+r\chi,$$
with brackets of weight $\tfrac12$. The full flux covector satisfies
$q_j=qU_j+r\nabla_UU_j$, since $\nabla_iU^i=\chi$ in the acceleration-free
gauge. In particular $q=0$ and $\nabla_UU=0$ imply $q_j=0$ even where $r=0$.
This normalization uses the coefficient $r$ of the source tensor and does
not divide by $r$ or $\kappa$.

**(d) Zero quantities and reduced premises.** Write
$\mathcal T^i{}_{jk}:=\Theta^i(e_j,e_k)$, also denoted $T^i{}_{jk}$ when
unambiguous; this torsion tensor is distinct from the stress-energy tensor.
The **zero quantities** are
$$z:=\bigl(\mathcal T^i{}_{jk},\ \Delta^i{}_{jkl},\ F_{jkl},\ q_j\bigr).$$
The reduced transport equations impose only
$\mathcal T^i{}_{0a}=0$ and $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$, and density transport imposes
$q=0$; the gauge gives $\nabla_UU=0$. Weyl evolution imposes the symmetric
spatial evolution projections of $F$. The reduced evolution does not itself
impose every component of $z=0$. The subsidiary theorem propagates the
remaining zero quantities from constrained initial data.

For vector-valued forms define $D_\omega\alpha=d\alpha+\omega\wedge\alpha$;
for an endomorphism-valued $k$-form define
$D_\omega\alpha=d\alpha+\omega\wedge\alpha-(-1)^k\alpha\wedge\omega$, with
matrix multiplication of endomorphism indices. These conventions specify the
Cartan identities used in [[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

items.title: The symmetric-tensor curl symbol is skew-adjoint with norm at most the wave number, giving positivity of the dust principal block
items.statement:
Let $V$ be the real vector space of symmetric $3\times3$ matrices with the
positive Frobenius product $\langle B,B'\rangle=B^{ij}B'_{ij}$, and for
$\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ define
$$C(\xi):V\to V,\qquad (C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l ,$$
with indices raised and lowered by the Euclidean metric and $\epsilon$ the
Levi-Civita symbol on the spatial frame of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Then:

**(a)** $C(\xi)$ is skew-adjoint: $\langle C(\xi)B,B'\rangle=-\langle B,C(\xi)B'\rangle$;

**(b)** $\|C(\xi)\|\le|\xi|$ for the operator norm induced by the Frobenius
product;

**(c)** the block operator $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
on $V\oplus V$ is symmetric (self-adjoint) with operator norm at most $|\xi|$;

**(d)** if $\zeta$ is a covector with $\zeta(U)=z$ and spatial part
$\zeta_\perp$, the symbol matrix
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}zI&C(\zeta_\perp)\\-C(\zeta_\perp)&zI\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
is positive definite whenever $z>|\zeta_\perp|$, in particular for every
future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$. Thus the coupled electric/magnetic
Weyl principal block has a positive time matrix on every spacelike initial
surface. This is a statement about that block; it makes no assertion here
about the other evolution equations of the full reduced dust system.

items.title: Reconstruction of a Weyl tensor from its electric and magnetic parts: symmetries, trace-freeness and recovery
items.statement:
Work in the frame conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and let $E_{ij},B_{ij}$ be
symmetric spatial tracefree fields, that is $E_{ij}U^j=B_{ij}U^j=0$ and $h^{ij}E_{ij}=h^{ij}B_{ij}=0$. Define $C$ by the
reconstruction formula of
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]] clause (d). Then:

**(a)** $C_{ijkl}$ is antisymmetric in $(i,j)$ and in $(k,l)$, symmetric under
the exchange of the pairs $(ij)\leftrightarrow(kl)$, satisfies the first
Bianchi (cyclic) identity $C_{i[jkl]}=0$, and is trace-free in every pair of
contracted indices;

**(b)** the electric and magnetic parts of $C$ with respect to $U$ are
$C_{0i0j}=E_{ij}$ and $C^*{}_{0i0j}=B_{ij}$;

**(c)** consequently if $E,B$ are in addition trace-free with respect to $h$,
then $C$ is a Weyl tensor and the map $(E,B)\mapsto C$ is a bijection onto the
Weyl tensors with the given $U$-electric and $U$-magnetic parts.

items.title: Local existence of Sobolev and classical solutions of a periodic symmetric hyperbolic system, uniform on bounded H^s data
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

items.title: The harmonic gauge vector, the reduced Einstein equation and the Einstein residual
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be an open set carrying a fixed smooth **background metric**
$\bar g$ with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose Christoffel
symbols in any chart are $\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the same symbol
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ denotes those of $g$. Let $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
be constants and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), the **matter stress-energy
tensor**, with $T=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ its metric trace
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Gauge vector.** The **harmonic-gauge vector field** of the pair
$(g,\bar g)$ is the smooth vector field
$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\bigr) .$$
The difference of the connection coefficients is a $(1,2)$-tensor, so $H$ is a
well-defined smooth vector field independent of the chart used to express the
symbols ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Reduced Einstein equation.** The **reduced Einstein equation** for the
pair $(g,T)$ with respect to $\bar g$ is the second-order quasilinear system
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\kappa\bigl(T_{ab}-\tfrac12Tg_{ab}\bigr)+\Lambda g_{ab},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ is the Ricci tensor of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]),
$H_b=g_{bc}H^c$ and $\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a)$.

**(c) Reduced solutions.** A **reduced solution** on $U$ is a pair $(g,T)$ of a
smooth Lorentzian metric and a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $U$ satisfying
(b) for the fixed background $\bar g$.

**(d) Einstein residual.** The **Einstein residual** of a pair $(g,T)$ is the
smooth symmetric $2$-tensor
$$E_{ab}:=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab},$$
with $S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ the scalar curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The pair solves the Einstein
equation exactly when $E=0$.

**(e) Constraint equations.** If $g$ is defined on a neighborhood of a spacelike
hypersurface $\Sigma$ with future unit normal field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential
frame $(e_i)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), the
**constraint residuals** are the functions $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)$ and
$E(\mathfrak n,e_i)$ on $\Sigma$; that these are the normal and
normal-tangential projections of the field equation, and that they agree with
the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations of the initial data, is
recorded in [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] and
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]].

The definition introduces the objects only. The principal part of (b), its
first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction, the identity expressing $E$ through
$H$, the wave equation satisfied by $H$ and the propagation of the constraint
residuals are proved in [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]],
[[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]],
[[lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity]] and
[[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]].

items.title: The reduced dust evolution equations: Weyl system, trace preservation, transport equations and symmetric hyperbolicity
items.statement:
Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] with $q:=U(r)+r\chi=0$ (the
dust continuity equation in the comoving gauge) and let $E,B$ be the
electric-magnetic variables of
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Then:

**(a) [Weyl evolution]** the reduced Weyl equations are
$$0=P_{ij}=\mathcal L_UE_{ij}+D_kB_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-3\chi_{(i}{}^lE_{j)l}-2\chi^l{}_{(i}E_{j)l}+h_{ij}\chi^{kl}E_{kl}+2\chi E_{ij}+\tfrac12\kappa r\bigl(\chi_{(ij)}-\tfrac13\chi h_{ij}\bigr),$$
$$0=Q_{ij}=\mathcal L_UB_{ij}-D_kE_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-\chi^l{}_{(i}B_{j)l}-2\chi_{(i}{}^lB_{j)l}+\chi B_{ij}+\chi^{kl}B^{pq}\epsilon_{pk(i}\epsilon_{qlj)},$$
where $\mathcal L_U$ is the Lie derivative along $U$ and the bracket on the
indices $i,j$ has weight $\tfrac12$; they are obtained by projecting the
Bianchi identity of the prescribed curvature onto the symmetric tracefree
spatial parts, the density-derivative terms cancelling by $q=0$;

**(b) [trace preservation]** extend the displayed symmetric equations of (a) algebraically to all symmetric spatial $E,B$. Contracting this extension with $h^{ij}$ gives $U(t_E)+2\chi t_E=0$ and $U(t_B)=0$, where $t_T=h^{ij}T_{ij}$. Thus
$h^{ij}E_{ij}$ and $h^{ij}B_{ij}$ satisfy homogeneous transport equations along
$U$; consequently zero initial traces remain zero, and the evolution may be
restricted to the five-dimensional tracefree space;

**(c) [transport equations]** with the parallel-comoving gauge one has
$$\partial_se_a{}^\mu=-\Gamma_a{}^j{}_0e_j{}^\mu,\qquad \partial_s\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j=R^{\mathrm{pre}\,i}{}_{j0a}-\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j\Gamma_a{}^k{}_0,\qquad \partial_sr=-r\chi,$$
the first two expressing zero time torsion and zero time-curvature residual, the
third the continuity equation; for tentative data the frame bracket is used in
the curvature definition so that these hold identically;

**(d) [symmetric hyperbolicity]** using the algebraic connection variables
$\chi_{ij}$ of [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]], equations (a)
and (c) form a first-order quasilinear system for
$(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$. In the parallel-comoving
frame, the equations for $(e,\Gamma,r)$ in (c) have only the transport
derivative $U=\partial_s$ as their principal derivative. The $E,B$ block has
time symbol $zI$ and spatial curl symbol
$$J(\xi)=\begin{pmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad (C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l,$$
with the positive Frobenius product on symmetric spatial tensors. By
[[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]], $J(\xi)$ is symmetric and
$\|J(\xi)\|\le|\xi|$. Thus for a future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$,
whose components satisfy $z:=\zeta(U)>|\zeta_\perp|$, the full principal symbol
is block diagonal with transport block $zI$ and Weyl block
$zI+J(\zeta_\perp)$, both positive definite. Hence the entire reduced dust
system is symmetric hyperbolic on every spacelike initial surface, including a
tilted one.

items.title: Gauss-Codazzi decomposition in Gaussian normal coordinates and the constraint equations in terms of the induced metric and second fundamental form
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

items.title: Uniqueness of classical solutions and continuous dependence in H^{s-1} for periodic symmetric hyperbolic systems
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$.

**(a) Uniqueness.** Let $J\ni0$ be an open interval and let
$u,v:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be classical solutions of
$(\star)$ in the sense of clause (d) of
[[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]], both taking values in $K$ and
satisfying $\sup_{t\in J}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, $\sup_{t\in J}\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$.
If $u(0)=v(0)$, then $u=v$ on $J$.

**(b) Continuous dependence.** Let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'$ and let $T>0$ be a time for which the existence
theorem [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] produces solutions
from every datum with values in $K$ and norm at most $R$, with values in $K'$
and the bounds $C(1+R)$ of that theorem. Then for all such data $u_0,v_0$ with
solutions $u,v$
$$\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C'\,e^{C'|t|}\,\|u_0-v_0\|_{H^{s-1}}\qquad(|t|<T),$$
with $C'=C'(A^\mu,B,K',R,s)$, the fixed compact coefficient time slab containing $[-T,T]$ being included in the coefficient data.

items.title: Harmonic initial data from geometric data: prescribing the metric jet of a spacelike slice in a time-independent background
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$
Then:

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

items.title: Subsidiary system of the dust reduction: Cartan identities, closed homogeneous residual system and vanishing of the residuals
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), carrying the analytic uniqueness and causal-curve supplier hypotheses.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the smooth time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime of [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]], with $\gamma=-g$, and let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be an open solution region. Let a smooth reduced dust solution on $\Omega$ have a nondegenerate tentative orthonormal frame for $\gamma$ of signature $(+---)$, a metric-compatible tentative connection, reconstructed algebraic Weyl tensor $C$, prescribed curvature $\overline R$, and dust Schouten tensor $S$ as in [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Let $\Sigma\subseteq\Omega$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface for $g$, with future unit normal $\mathfrak n$. Interpret the metric domain relative to $\Omega$: $D_\Omega^+(\Sigma)$ consists of points in $\Omega$ such that every past-inextendible causal curve in $\Omega$ through the point meets $\Sigma$, and $D_\Omega^-(\Sigma)$ is defined with future-inextendible curves ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (d), with $\Omega$ as ambient region). Allow $r\geq0$, with a smooth unit timelike $U$ prescribed also where $r=0$. Assume the parallel-comoving gauge and precisely the reduced equations
$$e_0=U,\quad\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0,\quad T^i{}_{0a}=0,\quad\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0,\quad P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=0,\quad q=U(r)+r\chi=0.$$
Here $a,b=1,2,3$, the first torsion index is the output index, and $P_{ab},Q_{ab}$ are the symmetric tracefree evolution projections of [[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]]. No spatial torsion or spatial curvature residual is assumed zero. Define $F_{jkl}=\nabla^i(C_{ijkl}-\gamma_{i[k}S_{l]j})$, $P_a=F_{0a0}$, and $Q_a=-\epsilon_a{}^{bc}F_{0bc}/2$. Then the spatial components of $(T,\Delta)$ and the vectors $(P,Q)$ satisfy the explicit closed linear homogeneous system constructed in the proof. Its principal part is transport along $U$ for $T,\Delta$ and the curl pair
$$e_0(P_a)+\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(Q_c),\qquad e_0(Q_a)-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(P_c).$$
It is symmetric hyperbolic on every spacelike initial hypersurface, including one tilted relative to $U$. If all residuals vanish initially, they vanish on the metric domain of determination of that surface relative to $\Omega$, namely $D_\Omega^+(\Sigma)\cup D_\Omega^-(\Sigma)$ as in [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], with causal curves taken inside the open solution region $\Omega$. Consequently the tentative connection is Levi--Civita, its actual curvature equals $\overline R$, and the resulting metric satisfies the full Einstein-dust equation. The conclusion uses neither division by $r$ nor hypersurface orthogonality of $U$.

items.title: Smooth data give smooth solutions of a periodic symmetric hyperbolic system on the existence interval
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the data class $\mathcal S(K,R)$. Let $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
take values in $K$ and satisfy $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then the solution $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0H^{s-1}$
of that theorem with $u(0)=u_0$ satisfies $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^m)$ and
$\partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{m-1})$ for every $m\ge s$, with bounds
depending only on $m$, $T$, $R$, the coefficient family, $K'$ and the $H^j$ bounds
of $u_0$ for $j\le m$; consequently $u\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$
and solves $(\star)$ classically.

items.title: Dust initial data: curvature and connection from (h,K), and the tilted constrained initialization of the Bianchi residuals
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), carrying the analytic uniqueness and causal-curve supplier hypotheses.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth spacelike initial surface with smooth induced Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_XN,Y)$, rest-mass density $\rho_{\rm mass}\ge0$, fixed $c>0$, and a prescribed smooth future $\gamma$-unit velocity $U_0$, where $\gamma=-g$ has signature $(+---)$. Put $\varepsilon=\rho_{\rm mass}c^2$. Assume the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the initial stress tensor $T_0=\varepsilon U_0^{\flat_g}\otimes U_0^{\flat_g}$, coupling $\kappa>0$ and cosmological constant $\Lambda$. The two lowered factors give the same covariant tensor with $\gamma=-g$. Choose an orientation and oriented tetrads locally for the magnetic contractions. Then locally:

(a) Gauss/Codazzi and the spatial target Ricci equations determine a unique full algebraic curvature tensor. Its full proper Lorentz basis transformation to an oriented tetrad with $e_0=U_0$, followed by the observer electric and magnetic contractions, determines $E_0,B_0$. Boosts may mix these parts.

(b) The tangential metric connection from $(h,K)$, differentiated boost data, and $\omega(U_0)=0$ uniquely determine the entire initial tetrad connection.

(c) At the first jets supplied by the reduced system, every initial torsion, curvature, matter-conservation and Bianchi residual vanishes. In particular the required direction-slot projections are $T^i{}_{0a}=0$ and $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$.

(d) For a future-positive timelike initial conormal $\zeta$, $z=\zeta(U_0)>|w|$ with $w_a=\zeta(e_a)$, the remaining Bianchi components obey $zP+\tfrac12w\times Q=0$, $zQ-\tfrac12w\times P=0$, so vanish. The initial time matrices are positive for every tilt $|v|<1$. Vacuum points remain admitted with prescribed auxiliary velocity.

items.title: The Einstein residual through the gauge vector, and the subsidiary wave equation satisfied by the gauge vector
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, let $\bar g$ be a smooth background
metric, let $H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the
harmonic-gauge vector and let $E_{ab}=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab}$ be
the Einstein residual of a smooth symmetric tensor $T$
([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]). Then:

**(a)** On every open set where $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation, the identity
$$E_{ab}=\tfrac12\bigl(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a-g_{ab}\nabla_cH^c\bigr)$$
holds on that set; and

**(b)** if $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on an open set $U$ and
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, then the gauge vector satisfies the homogeneous
linear wave equation
$$\Box_gH_b+\operatorname{Ric}_{ba}H^a=0\qquad\text{on }U,$$
where $\Box_gH_b=\nabla^a\nabla_aH_b$.

items.title: Principal part of the reduced Einstein operator and its first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $\bar g$
be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1},\bar g$
and the background curvature. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$ and $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=\mathcal C_{abi}$, where $\mathcal C_{abi}=-\bar R^c{}_{a0i}g_{cb}-\bar R^c{}_{b0i}g_{ac}$. Second covariant derivatives include their derivative-slot connection. These known background-curvature terms are zeroth order in the first-order state and vanish for the flat coordinate background. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(u;\bar g)\Bigr],$$
and the resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric.

items.title: Local well-posedness and finite-speed independence of the extension for symmetric hyperbolic systems on a coordinate neighbourhood
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the class $\mathcal S(K,R)$; for every datum $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ let $u$ be
the solution produced there on $(-T,T)$ with values in $K'$. Then:

**(a) [local existence]** For every $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ and every
$x_0\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the solution $u$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of
$(0,x_0)$ in $(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and solves $(\star)$ pointwise
there.

**(b) [finite speed / independence of the extension]** Let $\lambda_0>0$ be
determined by the coefficient bounds on a compact set containing the values of
the solutions in the following sense: for a truncated cone
$$D:=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ d(x,x_0)\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$$
with $t_0<T$, $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, lying in a single chart of $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$
in which the coordinate representation of $A^\mu$ satisfies
$\lambda\,A^0+\xi_iA^i\ge0$ for all unit $\xi$ (which holds for $\lambda$ large
enough by clause (a) of [[lem-gr-finite-speed-independence-of-extension]]),
let $u,v$ be solutions of two periodic symmetric hyperbolic systems whose
coefficient functions agree on a neighborhood of $D$ in the independent variables and on one common open state set containing both solution ranges, with
$u(0,\cdot)=v(0,\cdot)$ on the ball $\{d(x,x_0)\le\lambda t_0\}$. Then
$u=v$ on $D$.

**(c) [local uniqueness and stability]** If two classical solutions of the same
system on a common interval have values in $K$, $H^s$ norms at most $R$ and the
same initial value, they coincide; and the continuous-dependence estimate of
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] clause (b) holds
for the solutions of clause (a).

items.title: The barotropic fluid equations in enthalpy form are symmetric hyperbolic with positive principal symbol
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the enthalpy integral. Fix a smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ satisfying $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$. Fix the integration reference in the enthalpy variable $r$ of [[def-gr-barotropic-enthalpy-variable]], and put $c_s=\sqrt{p'}$. Let $u$ be the future unit fluid velocity, $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then:

**(a)** The full fluid equations are equivalent to
$$Dr+c_s\vartheta=0,\qquad \nabla_u u^b+c_s\Pi^{ba}\partial_ar=0.$$
The fluid stress $T^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab}$ is divergence-free precisely when these fluid equations hold.

**(b)** For variations $\eta=(\delta r,\delta u)$ with $g(u,\delta u)=0$, the smooth symmetric principal bilinear form at a covector $\zeta$ is
$$Q_\zeta(\eta,\eta')=\zeta(u)\left[\delta r\delta r'+g(\delta u,\delta u')\right]+c_s\left[\delta r\zeta(\delta u')+\delta r'\zeta(\delta u)\right].$$
For every timelike covector positively evaluated on future timelike vectors, it is positive definite. In a rest orthonormal basis it has eigenvalues $\zeta(u)$ twice and $\zeta(u)\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$, where $\zeta=-\zeta(u)u^\flat+\zeta_\perp$. Smooth velocity coordinates turn this bilinear form into actual smooth symmetric coefficient matrices.

**(c)** Appending the harmonic reduced Einstein metric block gives a smooth coupled first-order symmetric hyperbolic family on a local open admissible state set, with zeroth-order coupling in derivatives of the first-order variables. In an initially orthogonal chart, complete fluid data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, or the corresponding bundle velocity $U_0=W_0(N+v_0)$, $W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$ in $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$. They initialize $r=r(\epsilon_0)$, $u^0=W_0$ and $u^i=W_0v_0^i$. Normalization is enforced by reconstruction, and a reduced solution recovers the full fluid equations and conserved stress before imposing Einstein's unreduced equations. Every full fluid solution extracts to the same system. No vanishing-sound-speed or dust conclusion is asserted.

items.title: Symmetric hyperbolic reduction of the Einstein-scalar system and on-shell conservation
items.statement:
Fix one scalar model with smooth potential $V$ and fixed stress normalization $K_\phi$ as in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]. On a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold its equations and stress are
$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad T_{ab}=K_\phi\left[\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi-g_{ab}\left(\tfrac12g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\partial_d\varphi+V(\varphi)\right)\right].$$
Fix a chart and a smooth background $\bar g$ for the reduced Einstein equation of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. On the open state set where $g^{00}<0$ and $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite, the reduced Einstein equation coupled to this scalar equation has a smooth first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction with variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},\varphi,P=\partial_0\varphi,Q_i=\partial_i\varphi).$$
The time matrix is block diagonal with metric block $\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ and scalar block $\operatorname{diag}(1,-g^{00},g^{ij})$. Matter and metric cross-coupling is zeroth order in derivatives of $z$. The partial-derivative metric variables and the background-covariant ones are related by an invertible smooth zeroth-order change of variables; either gives the reduction.

For complete initial scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ in an initially orthogonal chart with $\partial_0=n$, prescribe $(\varphi,P,Q_i)=(\varphi_0,\pi_0,\partial_i\varphi_0)$. The auxiliary constraints propagate, the reconstructed scalar solves its full equation on the reduced metric, and its stress is conserved there before imposing the unreduced Einstein equation. Conversely every smooth physical scalar solution extracts to the same system. No potential positivity or mass sign is required; local arguments do not require a global orientation.

items.title: Propagation of the harmonic gauge and of the Einstein constraints: a constrained reduced solution is an Einstein solution
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), carrying the hypotheses of the analytic suppliers used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

items.title: Local existence for the reduced Einstein equation from Cauchy data on a spacelike slice
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), carrying the hypotheses of the analytic suppliers used below.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold carrying a chart $(x^0=t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ whose
domain $U$ contains the slice $\Sigma:=\{t=0\}$, let $\bar g$ be a smooth
background metric on $U$ with its Levi--Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $U$ together with the
background-covariant derivatives needed below (the matter field data). Suppose
smooth functions $g^0_{ab},g^1_{ab}$ on $\Sigma\cap U$ are given such that:

1. $g^0$ is a smooth field of Lorentzian bilinear forms on the restricted
   spacetime tangent bundle $TM|_{\Sigma\cap U}$, whose restriction to
   $T\Sigma$ is positive definite. Write $g^0_{ab}$ for its components in the
   given spacetime chart; its inverse components satisfy $g^{00}_0<0$ and the
   spatial block $(g_0^{ij})$ is positive definite;
2. $g^1_{ab}$ is symmetric and agrees on $\Sigma$ with the components of
   $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ for some smooth extension $g$ of $g^0$ to $U$;
3. the harmonic-gauge condition $H^a=0$ holds on $\Sigma\cap U$ for the pair
   $(g,\bar g)$ ([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]).

Then there is an open neighborhood $V\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma\cap U$ and a smooth
metric $g$ on $V$ with $g|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^0$ and
$\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^1_{ab}$, solving the **reduced Einstein
equation** with the given background $\bar g$ and matter tensor $T$
([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]) on $V$.
