items.title: Local geometric uniqueness for a fixed covariant Einstein-matter model with complete data
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth tensor fields $\Psi$, specified equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$, and a specified stress expression $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Covariance means pullback by a local diffeomorphism commutes with these equations and stress expression. Fix complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$ for this model, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric tensor $K$ on a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$, with $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal.

The following explicit harmonic-reduction hypothesis is required. On each relatively compact initial coordinate ball, with flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, specify finite first-order variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w),$$
fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules for $w,\Psi$, and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$, shared by both solutions, such that:

**(R1)** Every smooth solution of this same model written in harmonic coordinates has extracted variables satisfying
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_iA^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
where all $A^\mu$ are symmetric and $A^0$ is positive definite. Reconstruction recovers all matter fields and $T$ from $z$. Any internal matter gauge has already been fixed with its specified data and equations; otherwise the conclusion must include the appropriate internal gauge equivalence.
**(R2)** The initial value of $w$ is a specified smooth expression $\mathcal I(h,K,d)$ in the full data in this coordinate gauge. Thus $d$ determines every initial first-order variable, not merely initial stress tensor jets.
**(R3)** After shrinking a closed cylinder, both state ranges lie in one compact convex subset of $O$, coefficient first derivatives are bounded and $A^0\ge aI$ for some $a>0$.

These are PDE and extraction hypotheses, not an assumption of geometric uniqueness. Let $(M,g,\Psi,j)$ and $(M',g',\Psi',j')$ be two smooth time-oriented developments of this same model, solving the same Einstein equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$ and the same matter equations, whose spacelike embeddings induce $(h,K,d)$. Then near each initial point there is a smooth time-orientation-preserving isometry $\Phi$ with $\Phi\circ j=j'$ on the initial patch, $\Phi^*\Psi'=\Psi$ and consequently $\Phi^*T'=T$. Its germ along the initial patch is unique. These germs glue to one such isometry between open neighborhoods of the entire embedded initial surfaces. No uniform collar width or global-in-time assertion is made.

references.title: Friedrich and Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, sections 3.1-3.2, 5.1-5.2 and 5.4

items.title: Local geometric development for a fixed covariant Einstein-matter model with complete constrained data
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

references.title: Friedrich and Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, sections 3.1-3.2, 5.1-5.2 and 5.4

items.title: Local evolution for a strict barotropic perfect fluid: smooth constrained data admit a development, unique up to a data-fixing isometry
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$, density $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and tangent field $v_0$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$. These specify the future unit initial velocity
$$U_0=W_0(N+v_0),\qquad W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$$
in $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for
$$T_0=(\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0))U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}+p(\epsilon_0)g_0.$$
Then a smooth time-oriented local development has metric $g$, density $\epsilon$ and future unit fluid velocity $u$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left[(\epsilon+p)u_au_b+pg_{ab}\right],\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+\Pi^{ba}\partial_ap=0.$$
Here $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$. Initial geometric data are $(h,K_2)$ and initial matter data are $(\epsilon_0,U_0)$ under $N\mapsto n$, $X\mapsto i_*X$. Arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt is allowed. The initial surface lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence; its interior Cauchy neighborhood is globally hyperbolic. Any two developments of this same EOS and complete data agree near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing future isometry matching density and velocity. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; shocks, vacuum boundaries and vanishing sound speed are outside this strict interior-fluid statement ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

items.title: Local Einstein-dust evolution: smooth constrained data with prescribed velocity admit a smooth local development, unique up to a data-fixing isometry
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix constants $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and a smooth mass-normalized density $\rho_0\ge0$. Specify initial velocity as a smooth section $U_0$ of $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with the bundle metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, satisfying $g_0(U_0,U_0)=-1$ and positive $N$ coefficient. Thus the velocity need not be normal and does not presuppose a spacetime development. Put $\varepsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ and require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for $T_0=\varepsilon_0U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}$. On $\{\rho_0>0\}$ this is exactly the dust supplier with density parameter $\varepsilon_0$, rather than $\rho_0$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); zero regions have independently prescribed velocity.

Then there is a smooth local development: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian metric $g$, density $\rho\ge0$ and future unit timelike field $u$ near an embedded copy of $\Sigma$, solving
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\rho c^2u_au_b,\qquad \nabla_uu=0,\qquad u(\rho)+\rho\nabla\!\cdot u=0.$$
The induced geometric and matter data are $(h,K,\rho_0,U_0)$, with $\mathcal V$ identified by $aN+X\mapsto an+i_*X$ using the future unit normal $n$. The initial surface lies in the interior of its domain of dependence; restriction to its Cauchy neighborhood gives a local Cauchy development. Every two such developments agree near $\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\rho,u$. No division by density is used, so smooth empty regions are admitted. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; no uniform noncompact slab or continuation past flow crossings is asserted.

items.title: Local Einstein-scalar evolution: smooth constrained data admit a local development, unique up to a data-fixing isometry
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one scalar model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], with its fixed smooth potential and normalization. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$ and complete scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$. Suppose the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold for the scalar stress computed from these data, with $\pi_0$ the prescribed future-normal derivative. Then there is a smooth local Einstein-scalar development
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad \Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,$$
with induced geometric data $(h,K_2)$, $\varphi|_\Sigma=\varphi_0$ and $n(\varphi)|_\Sigma=\pi_0$. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width. The initial surface is interior to its intrinsic domain of dependence; restricting to the interior Cauchy neighborhood gives a globally hyperbolic development. Every two developments of this same fixed model and complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\varphi$. No potential positivity, mass sign, global existence or uniform noncompact slab is asserted ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

items.title: High-regularity local developments for the selected matter sectors: vacuum with Lambda, scalar, strict barotropic fluid and geodesic dust
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and $c>0$ be constants, let $\Sigma$ be a smooth
three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and symmetric $2$-tensor $K$,
and suppose smooth matter initial data and a matter sector are given in one of
the following four branches, with the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] satisfied:

1. **vacuum with cosmological constant:** no matter fields; the constraints
   read $S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$;
2. **scalar field:** a model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ as in
   [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential and initial data
   $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$;
3. **strict barotropic perfect fluid:** a model with smooth $p=p(\epsilon)$ and
   $\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$, with initial data
   $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, equivalently the abstract bundle velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(N+v_0)$, as specified in [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]];
4. **geodesic dust:** an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon_0\ge0$
   with prescribed smooth future unit velocity $U_0$, as a section of
   $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $-ab+h(X,Y)$.
   On positive-density regions this is the model $(\varepsilon,u)$ of
   [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; through zero-density regions its smooth
   unit velocity is separately prescribed and required to remain geodesic.
   Its source is $T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$.

Then in each branch there is a smooth local development with the properties
established in the corresponding item, [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]
(branch 2), [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] (branch 3),
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] (branch 4) and, for branch 1, the vacuum
instance of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g$ with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data $(h,K)$, solving
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ with the branch's stress tensor and matter
equations, with $\Sigma$ in the interior of its domain of dependence, and with
uniqueness near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

items.title: Local Cauchy development of the adopted Einstein field law for smooth constrained data in the selected matter sectors
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

Adopt the direct-equation presentation of the classical gravitational framework
for a model satisfying the spacetime and classical-domain postulate
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the field-and-matter postulate
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], with the field law
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]: on the matter domain of the model,
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab},\qquad \kappa=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4},$$
with $T$ the stress-energy tensor of the model's selected matter sector. Let the
sector be one of:

1. vacuum with cosmological constant ($T=0$);
2. the scalar-field model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]
   with a chosen smooth potential whose scalar equation and stress tensor are
   those defined there, writing $K_\phi$ for that definition's scalar normalization constant;
3. the perfect-fluid model of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] with a
   smooth barotropic equation of state satisfying $\epsilon+p>0$ and
   $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ on the range of the data;
4. an energy-coefficient dust density $\varepsilon\ge0$ and prescribed
   smooth future unit velocity, with $T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$.
   On positive-density regions this is [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]];
   on zero-density regions the velocity is separately prescribed and the
   geodesic equation remains imposed. Equivalently the mass-normalized
   density is $\rho=\varepsilon/c^2$.

Use the SI and coordinate conventions of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]: in a length-coordinate chart
$x^0=ct$, the metric is dimensionless, $[c]=\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, $[\Lambda]=\mathrm m^{-2}$,
$[G_N]=\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, and
$[\kappa]=\mathrm m^{-1}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^2$, so $\kappa T$
has curvature units. Every velocity denoted $u$ in this theorem is normalized
by $g(u,u)=-1$. Its SI proper-time four-velocity is $U_{\rm SI}=cu$, with
$g(U_{\rm SI},U_{\rm SI})=-c^2$; the initial $U_0$ in the mathematical bundle
formulation is normalized, and its SI counterpart is $cU_0$. The mass-normalized density is $\rho=\rho_{\rm mass}:=\varepsilon/c^2$ with
units $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The dust source uses
$\varepsilon=\rho_{\rm mass}c^2$ and
$\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat=\rho_{\rm mass}U_{\rm SI}^\flat\otimes
U_{\rm SI}^\flat$; fluid $\epsilon$ and $p$ have units
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $p'$ is dimensionless. For the scalar branch
choose an arbitrary field unit $\Phi$ and use $[\varphi]=\Phi$,
$[V]=\Phi^2\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $[K_\phi]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-1}\,\Phi^{-2}$;
then $\Box_g\varphi$ and $V'(\varphi)$ have units $\Phi\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and
$T_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$.

Let $(\Sigma,h,K)$ with the sector's smooth initial data (respectively nothing,
$(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$, $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$, $(\varepsilon_0,U_0)$) satisfy the constraint
equations [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the sector's
stress tensor. Here fluid $v_0\in\Gamma(T\Sigma)$ obeys $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, with full initial unit velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(N+v_0)$ in $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, exactly as in [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]]. Then the model admits a **local Cauchy development**: there are
a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of the framework and
a spacelike embedded image of $\Sigma$ inducing $(h,K)$ and the stated matter
data, solving the field law $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ and the
sector's matter equations on a neighborhood of $\Sigma$; $\Sigma$ lies in the
interior of its domain of dependence; and any two such developments of the same
data agree near $\Sigma$ up to an isometry fixing the data and the time
orientation. The development is local in time and no uniform-in-the-data
existence time or global statement is asserted.
items.physical_scope: Classical general relativity in the smooth high-regularity branch: four-dimensional smooth Lorentzian geometry of signature (-+++), cosmological constant Lambda, and one of the classical matter sectors — vacuum, a scalar field with smooth potential, a strict barotropic perfect fluid with 0<p'<1, or geodesic dust — with smooth constrained initial data; the conclusion is a local-in-time development before any flow crossing. It makes no statement about nature, global or all-time existence, nonsmooth or distributional sources, shocks, free-boundary or junction behavior, asymptotic regimes, or an optimal Sobolev threshold. Smooth zero sets and empty regions are included in the dust branch with its separately prescribed smooth geodesic velocity.

items.title: Scope and status of the Gr14 high-regularity symmetric hyperbolic material
items.statement:
This page contains the Gr14 high-regularity symmetric hyperbolic proof material:
the periodic first-order theory (E0), the harmonic-gauge reduced Einstein
equation and its subsidiary system (E1), the geometric data and local
development theorems (E2), and the selected matter reductions with the complete
geodesic-dust residual chain (E3, E3d--E3d.2). Its content assumes Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for local analytic extraction and manifold patching, and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]) for the causal-curve calculus in the Cauchy-neighborhood argument. Its physical content is conditional:
the physical reading is the model deduction of
[[pthm-gr-high-regularity-local-development]] from the adopted postulates
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and the matter definitions
[[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; the mathematical carriers are
[[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] and its prerequisites.

**What is established.** Local-in-time smooth developments of the adopted field
law with the selected matter sectors, from smooth constrained data, with
uniqueness near the initial surface up to a data-fixing time-orientation-
preserving isometry, and with the initial surface lying in the interior of its
domain of dependence.

**What is not established or assumed away.** No global or all-time existence,
no uniform existence time on noncompact data, no maximality or boundary
behaviour of the development (that is the scope of the successor page), no
shocks, free boundaries, vacuum boundaries or junction conditions, no
distributional or low-regularity sources, no optimal Sobolev threshold (the
theorem works in the smooth/high-regularity branch with $s\ge5$), no
quantitative measurement or observational claim. For dust, the construction
occurs before flow crossings and the velocity is prescribed separately, so
empty regions with zero energy coefficient $\varepsilon=0$ are included and no division by density occurs. The source density parameter is $\varepsilon$, with mass-normalized $\rho=\varepsilon/c^2$ for every $c>0$; the
density solves $\partial_sr=-r\chi$ with the explicit exponential solution of
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]]. For the fluid branch the strict hypotheses
$\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'<1$ are essential; the failure at negative $p'$ is the
companion counterexample on the examples page. No statement is made that any
model here describes nature, and no empirical premise enters.

**Conventions and sources.** The reduction uses $\gamma=-g$ and the explicit Schouten normalization and curvature decomposition of its definition. Vacuum reduction signs therefore differ from the original metric signs by that constant flip. The local dust proof derives the electric/magnetic projections and the Cartan subsidiary system in those conventions; its magnetic double-epsilon term has the sign required by trace preservation. Friedrich and Rendall supplies derivation provenance; the displayed local arguments carry the deductions.

items.statement:

items.title: Worked E0 check: constant-coefficient transport on the three-torus, explicit solution and conserved energy
items.statement:
On $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ take $m=1$, $A^0=1$, $A^1=2$, $A^2=A^3=0$, $B=0$,
so the system $(\star)$ of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]
reads $\partial_tu+2\partial_1u=0$, with $u_0\in H^s$ real-valued and $s\ge5$.
This example exhibits the explicit solution on the periodic domain,
$u(t,x)=u_0(x^1-2t,x^2,x^3)$, verifies that it is the E0 solution, and checks
the weighted energy identity $e'(t)=0$ for the energy
$e(t)=\int u(t)^2\,d\mu$ directly.

items.title: A negative pressure derivative defeats fixed-Sobolev evolution: exponentially growing Fourier modes of the linearized barotropic fluid
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), carrying the integration hypothesis of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]].

Refuted statement: "At every constant rest state with $H_0=\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0)>0$, the fixed-flat-background linearized barotropic fluid equations admit a periodic $C^1$ solution on some positive time interval for every smooth periodic initial datum, and their solution operators are continuous in each fixed integer Sobolev topology $H^r$, $r\ge0$, at every fixed positive time."

For $p'(\epsilon_0)=-a^2<0$, both assertions fail: the explicit smooth datum of step 2.2 has no such solution on any positive time interval, and the smooth single-mode sequence of step 2.1 proves failure of $H^r$ continuity for every integer $r\ge0$ at every fixed positive time. These conclusions concern the specified linearized equations; nonlinear Einstein-fluid illposedness with constrained data remains an open prerequisite.

items.title: Worked fluid symbol: eigenvalues of the principal matrix for the radiation equation of state at an explicit timelike covector
items.statement:
Take the barotropic equation of state $p(\epsilon)=\tfrac13\epsilon$ (so
$c_s=1/\sqrt3$) and at a point choose a rest frame $n$ with spatial frame
$(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and the future-directed timelike covector
$\zeta=-n^\flat+\tfrac12 e_1^\flat$ (in the notation
$\zeta_0=\zeta(n)=1$, $\zeta_\perp=\tfrac12e_1$, so
$\zeta_0=1>\tfrac12=|\zeta_\perp|$).
This example computes the matrix $A(\zeta)$ of
[[lem-gr-barotropic-fluid-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]] and verifies its
eigenvalues and positive definiteness explicitly.
